issues.issue: What is the appropriate standard of review?
issues.applicant_position: Correctness for procedural fairness; reasonableness for review of the officer's evidence assessment.
issues.respondent_position: Reasonableness for points-based factual findings; correctness only for procedural fairness.
issues.result_quote: the appropriate standard of review for issues of procedural fairness and natural justice is correctness

issues.issue: Did the officer deny procedural fairness or act unreasonably by not explaining why the Canadian-relative evidence was insufficient?
issues.applicant_position: Officer erred by not explaining why the evidence on Canadian relatives was insufficient, making the decision unreasonable.
issues.respondent_position: Officer gave an explanation; the applicant bore the onus and the checklist required birth certificates.
issues.result_quote: I do not find that the officer erred by not explaining why the evidence that the applicant submitted for his relatives in Canada was insufficient.

issues.issue: Was the officer required to make further inquiries or give notice before rejecting the evidence?
issues.applicant_position: Officer should have interviewed him or notified him and allowed him to respond.
issues.respondent_position: Officer had no duty to make further inquiries; the onus rests on the applicant.
issues.result_quote: the officer was not required to ask for additional information of the applicant and the applicant was not denied procedural fairness

issues.issue: Should costs be awarded to the applicant?
issues.applicant_position: The officer's errors were egregious and warrant an award of costs.
issues.respondent_position: The applicant has not shown special reasons for costs.
issues.result_quote: I am not prepared to award costs as I am of the view that special reasons do not exist in this case
